## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Hemakamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Hemaka") constitutes the ninth discourse of the *Pārāyanavagga*, the fifth chapter of the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 5.9, PTS Snp 209) [Anderson & Smith 1913; SuttaCentral]. In the collection's sequential numbering, its verses begin at verse 1084, framing a dialogue in verse between the Buddha and the student Hemaka (*icc-āyasmā Hemako*) [Norman 1997–2001; Anderson & Smith 1913]. The text centers on the inquiry of how one crosses over entanglements and desire in the world [SuttaCentral].

In the traditional exegetical literature of the Pali canon, the sutta is preserved and analyzed word-by-word in the *Cullaniddesa*, specifically within the *Hemakamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 12) and the *Pucchā* (Cnd 2) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse data from DharmaNexus confirms this close canonical relationship, detecting 22 matching segments shared with Cnd 12 (with up to 97% similarity across §§ 2.4–4.4) and 5 matches with Cnd 2 (§§ 0.1–4.5, with 99% similarity) [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies any extant parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

Modern editions include the Pali Text Society edition edited by Dines Andersen and Helmer Smith, and it has been translated into English by scholars including H. Saddhatissa and Bhikkhu Sujato, with additional modern translations appearing in eleven other languages [Anderson & Smith 1913; Saddhatissa 2013; SuttaCentral].
